header.name: Neural Engineering and Implantable Devices
header.description: This course introduces the (senior undergraduate and graduate) students to the basics of neural engineering and how electrical engineering techniques can be applied to design medical solutions for neurological conditions. The course starts with the fundamentals of the nervous system, neural signal processing, and modeling neuronal response using equivalent electrical circuits. Then, it introduces the fast-expanding fields of neurotechnology, specifically brain-computer interfaces, neural prosthetic systems (such as artificial retina and peripheral neural stimulators), and wireless power transfer for implantable devices. Through simulation tools, the students will learn to simulate neuronal behavior, predict induced electric fields and resulting neural responses, and propose novel designs of neuroprosthetic systems.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Understand the basics of neural engineering and its role in modern healthcare. Explain the neural response using equivalent electric circuits.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Evaluate strengths and limitations of different neural stimulation modalities. Analyze design challenges of neuroprosthetic systems and propose novel solutions.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Analyze challenges in designing brain-computer interfaces and wireless power transfer techniques for implantable devices, and propose novel solutions.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Build models to simulate the neural behavior and predict induced electric fields. Design and characterize coils for WPT for implantable devices.

lecture_topics: Electrical signaling in nervous system - membrane as an RC circuit
